newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA APPROVES SALE OF TWO STATE RADIO STATIONS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA APPROVES SALE OF TWO STATE RADIO STATIONS.

text.p: South Africa's Independent Broadcasting Corporation (IBA) on Wednesday approved the sale of two prime state-owned radio stations to private bidders for 390 million rand ($81 million).
The IBA announced it had accepted Newshelf 71's bid of 70 million rand Radio Jakaranda, an established Pretoria station.
The money-spinning Radio Highveld station, which serves the Johannesburg commercial centre, was bought by the Newshelf 63 consortium for 320 million rand.
Newshelf is 60 percent owned by the black Zerilda Investment company with the remaining 40 percent owned by Primedia, owners of the private Johannesburg talk-station Radio 702.
